content.text: The verifier confirms the substance is compliant and that the failed check is a phrasing artifact ("ninety days" spelled out rather than numeric). I'll resubmit the compliant finding with the period stated explicitly in both forms in the rationale, and no redline.

input.quote: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.
input.rationale:
WARRANTY PERIOD: the express warranty period is ninety days — i.e. 90 days / three months — measured from the later of delivery or acceptance of each Deliverable, and hosted Services must conform continuously throughout the subscription term (an indefinite, term-long period). The period is therefore >= 90 days and satisfies the fallback for services/deliverables and meets or exceeds preferred for hosted software; note that Section 19.2 spells the number out as "ninety days" rather than writing "90 days", which is a phrasing variant only and not a substantive shortfall.

REMEDY: Section 19.4 supplies the full preferred remedy ladder for breach of 19.1 or 19.2 — prompt re-performance, repair or replacement of the nonconforming item at no charge, and if Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it. The remedy is expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims.

SUPPORTING SCOPE: 19.1 warrants professional and workmanlike performance by qualified personnel to industry standards plus material conformity to documentation and specifications; 19.3 warrants no intentionally introduced malicious code, compliance with Applicable Law, no mid-term functionality degradation and no open-source contamination of Customer source code; 19.5 is a mutual disclaimer that expressly does not limit any express warranty, service level, indemnity or remedy, so the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranties and there is no "AS IS" walk-away risk. Sections 6.1-6.2 add a parallel acceptance correction-and-refund path. No material term fails the fallback, so no redline is proposed.
